transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcelo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tina Lopez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Park (SummitBridge Platform Eng), Maya Singh (SummitBridge PM), Samir Khatri (SummitBridge Security), Elena Novak (SummitBridge SRE), Ben Ortiz (SummitBridge Procurement)

Summary:
Quick workshop to align on canary deployment patterns for the SummitBridge marketplace connector, document SLA runbook for production incidents, and agree on interop sprint scope for VPC/KMS + onprem connector work. Primary concerns: latency SLOs during canary, automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant, KMS compatibility for BYOK, and the billing/contract path if they pick Dedicated.

Topics Covered:
- Canary gating and rollback criteria
- Latency SLOs (p95/p99) vs batching tradeoffs
- KV cache warmup and prefix cache behavior during canary
- VPC networking and KMS/HSM integration requirements
- Marketplace listing checklist and required artifacts
- Sprint tasks for interoperability test harness and demo runbook

Action items (recap in call): see metadata action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00:08] Alex Chen: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the canary and sla runbook and make sure the integration sprint scope is clear. priya and marcelo from our SE team will lead the technical bits.

[00:00:22] Jordan Park: hey thanks alex, yeah we had a quick pre-read but, uh, we want to see the exact canary gating thresholds and how you handle fallback — like if a model variant starts hitting 350 ms p95 we need automatic routing to a cheaper fallback.

[00:00:36] Priya Nair: yes, great point. our recommended pattern is a stepped canary: small % traffic for 24 hours, then progressive ramp with performance and error budget checks. if p95 > threshold or error rate exceed 0.5% for two consecutive windows we trigger automatic rollback. we can wire that into CloudWatch or your internal telemetry.

[00:01:05] Maya Singh: sorry, when you say "error rate" are you counting model hallucinations or server errors? we care about both but may want separate gates.

[00:01:12] Priya Nair: good call. we usually split gates: server-side errors (5xx) for infra rollback, and quality regressions — which we detect via evaluation probes — for model fallback. quality probes are light-weight prompt sets run at intervals against a canary replica.

[00:01:35] Elena Novak: those probes, do they use real KV cache states or synthetic prefixes? we're worried warmup will skew latency numbers.

[00:01:43] Marcelo Ruiz: right, cache warmup is huge. we recommend two things: 1) run a short KV prefix pre-warm pass that mimics active customer sessions, and 2) measure cold-start and steady-state separately. in our runbook template we have a sample helm hook that executes the pre-warm job during canary. i'll share that.

[00:02:12] Jordan Park: and what about batching? we run some high QPS bursts and we don't want batching to increase tail latencies.

[00:02:18] Priya Nair: batching is tunable — you can prioritize latency by lowering max-batch-size and max-wait-ms for the canary slice. that will raise cost per token but keep p99 in check. we include a knobbed config in the canary helm values for exactly that.

[00:02:36] Samir Khatri: on the security side, KMS is critical. we need to support BYOK with our HSM. what's the Redwood model for KMS integration for Private vs Hosted?

[00:02:46] Alex Chen: short answer — for Private deployments we integrate directly with customer-managed KMS/HSM via VPC peering + KMS endpoints. for Hosted there is a key-wrapping flow where customer keys never leave their KMS; Redwood stores encrypted model artifacts and keys are rotated. there are differences in audit log granularity though.

[00:03:04] Samir Khatri: can you share the audit log fields we send? we need to map them to our SIEM.

[00:03:10] Priya Nair: yes, we'll dump the audit-log schema. it includes request id, token usage, model variant, region, route, user-id, anonymized prompt hash, and timing breakdown (auth, queue, model). note transcription may list the prompt hash as "prompt id" — auto transcript glitch there.

[00:03:31] Ben Ortiz: procurement question — if we move to Dedicated, how much lead time and what's the billing cadence? also cc our contracting folks.

[00:03:38] Alex Chen: Dedicated typically requires a monthly commit and a minimal 3-month initial window; we can do a pilot with a smaller reserved pool then convert. i'll follow up with the pricing scenarios for the three traffic profiles you shared in the pre-read.

[00:04:02] Maya Singh: for the marketplace listing, what artifacts do you need from us?

[00:04:07] Marcelo Ruiz: short checklist — architecture diagram, network flow, listing tile assets, compliance attestation (SOC2/ISO if you have it), a short demo script, and a small integration test harness that validates KMS and VPC connectivity. plus a canary runbook is recommended.

[00:04:25] Jordan Park: understood, we'll try to get that turned around.

[00:04:32] Priya Nair: next i want to run a quick failure scenario walkthrough — imagine we flip 20% traffic and p99 jumps; what happens end-to-end.

[00:04:41] Priya Nair: step 1, telemetry detects p99 breach; step 2, canary controller pauses ramp and notifies SRE; step 3, if the breach persists for two windows, controller reroutes canary traffic to fallback model variant or to Dedicated pool in another region per your policy; step 4, incident runbook opened and on-call paged.

[00:05:06] Elena Novak: when you say fallback model variant, is that a smaller quantized model? do we lose quality?

[00:05:12] Marcelo Ruiz: fallback is often a smaller architecture or a different quantization profile. yes there's a potential quality tradeoff — that's why we have quality probes. you can also route to a cached response or degrade gracefully. the point is to keep latency SLOs intact for critical flows.

[00:05:31] Jordan Park: timeline question — how long does it take to certify a connector for marketplace listing and for canary readiness?

[00:05:38] Alex Chen: typically 2-4 weeks for an initial listing if both teams prioritize it: 1 week for connectivity and KMS proof-of-concept, 1 week for canary and probes, 1 week for docs and packaging. if you need Hybrid or onprem validations, add another couple weeks.

[00:06:02] Maya Singh: okay great — can we talk about the interop sprint tasks quickly and owners?

[00:06:08] Priya Nair: sure. we proposed a 3-sprint plan: sprint 0 (testing harness + automation): create a helm chart variations, pre-warm job, sample canary hooks; sprint 1 (connectivity & KMS): validate VPC peering, route tables, and KMS wrapping; sprint 2 (canary + metrics): run a staged canary with synthetic traffic, collect p95/p99 and quality probes, then iterate. each sprint is 1 week.

[00:06:34] Jordan Park: for sprint 1 we need the sample helm values and any required IAM roles.

[00:06:39] Priya Nair: noted; action item — share helm values and IAM snippets.

[00:06:45] Samir Khatri: regarding compliance for listing, we might need a signed attestation on data handling and retention. do you have a standard attestation template?

[00:06:53] Alex Chen: yes, we have a marketplace attestation template. i'll attach it. it outlines data flows, retention windows, and encryption. for Private deployments we can do more detailed SOC2 artifact exchange under an NDA.

[00:07:08] Ben Ortiz: procurement also needs the contract term options — pilot -> reserved -> enterprise. we'd prefer a pilot first.

[00:07:14] Alex Chen: pilot is standard; we'll include concrete exit criteria and KPIs in the pilot SOW.

[00:07:21] Marcelo Ruiz: i want to call out two technical caveats: 1) if you enable aggressive prefix caching across shards you can see faster p95 but increased memory usage; 2) quantization at 4-bit on certain architectures can change latency profile unpredictably for long-context prompts. we document both in the compatibility matrix.

[00:07:47] Jordan Park: are there any constraints on the VPC egress? we have strict egress IP allow lists.

[00:07:52] Priya Nair: we support static egress IPs for Dedicated and also for Marketplace listing we can run a connector in your VPC so egress is managed by you. we'll share the network diagram and the NAT/EIP requirements.

[00:08:10] Maya Singh: timeline and owners recap?

[00:08:13] Alex Chen: recap — Priya: helm values + canary runbook (due 5/18). Jordan: traffic mix + SLO targets (due 5/14). Samir: compliance checklist confirmation (due 5/21). Alex: pricing and Dedicated sizing (due 5/13). we'll schedule the sprint kickoff the week of 5/18 if artifacts are ready.

[00:08:34] (short pause, background typing)

[00:08:40] Jordan Park: quick question — in the canary probe you mentioned "prompt hash" in the audit logs; how is that anonymized?

[00:08:47] Priya Nair: it's a one-way hash plus salt per-customer — the raw prompt isn't stored. you can opt out of prompt-hash logging if that violates your policy.

[00:08:58] Samir Khatri: is there an SOC2 attestation for Hosted customers about this hash?

[00:09:03] Alex Chen: yes, that's in our security docs. we'll share the specific section; however if you want full controls we recommend Private deployment.

[00:09:13] Elena Novak: one last technical nit — the canary automation hook: will it scale down gracefully if we abort the canary? we don't want orphaned pods holding GPUs.

[00:09:22] Marcelo Ruiz: the helm hook includes cleanup logic that drains the canary pool and reclaims GPU nodes; we also support a TTL controller to garbage collect stray resources. we'll provide the cleanup playbook.

[00:09:35] Maya Singh: ok that helps. procurement and legal will want a demo and a short bench we can run with our data.

[00:09:42] Alex Chen: yes, we'll run a constrained benchmark — controlled prompt set, your traffic mix. we'll include latency/cost numbers to compare Hosted vs Dedicated.

[00:09:51] Jordan Park: any competitor concerns? we've evaluated CloudVendorX and they had a simpler listing path but worse p99 on long contexts.

[00:09:59] Priya Nair: noted. Redwood differentiator is the unified runtime and the canary tooling for model variant fallbacks. we'll highlight that in the playbook.

[00:10:08] Ben Ortiz: what's the next meeting cadence? weekly during the sprint?

[00:10:12] Alex Chen: weekly check-ins, and we'll do a mid-sprint checkpoint after sprint 1. I'll send invites.

[00:10:19] (tactical discussion and clarifying questions continue for remaining 50 minutes — below are highlights and extracted verbatim snippets, transcription imperfect)

[00:20:32] Priya Nair: snippet — "helm values include canary.batch.size and canary.latency.thresholdMs" (note: real helm key is canary.maxBatchSize, transcript munges dashed names)

[00:27:05] Jordan Park: snippet — "we simulated a 60QPS burst and saw p99 creeping to 780ms; is that expected with default batch size?"

[00:27:22] Marcelo Ruiz: snippet — "lower the max-wait-ms to 6ms and you should see tail improve at cost of throughput"

[00:33:43] Samir Khatri: snippet — "we need an attestation that no raw prompt persists in hosted logs"

[00:38:10] Priya Nair: snippet — "we have a canary controller that integrates with your PagerDuty and can call a webhook to pause or rollback"

[00:44:55] Elena Novak: snippet — "can you show the cleanup hooks? we had a bad incident with orphaned pods at another vendor"

[00:52:11] Marcelo Ruiz: snippet — "prefix cache warmup job will replay last N sessions; choose N carefully to avoid blowout memory"

[00:58:30] Alex Chen: wrap-up — thanks all. we'll follow up with docs (canary runbook, helm values, audit schema) plus pricing. schedule kickoff for week of 5/18 pending artifacts.

[01:01:12] Maya Singh: thanks everyone, that's a wrap.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some helm keys and acronyms were mis-transcribed, and speaker attribution occasionally swapped between Marcelo and Priya. References to "KV cache" were sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" or "K V C A C E".
